Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

Overview

The Deputy Treasurer is a senior Treasury leader responsible for establishing the standards, frameworks, and management processes that support sound balance sheet decision-making, regulatory readiness, and effective risk oversight. The role reports to the Treasurer and initially serves as a functional leader across Treasury governance, enterprise capital and liquidity stress testing, and forward-looking balance sheet planning.

The position owns program design, methodology, governance, integration, challenge, and executive communication. The role will rely on subject matter experts and execution teams across Treasury, Finance, Risk Management, Investor Relations, Asset Liability Management, business units, and the Bank’s Shanghai team to implement approved standards and produce recurring deliverables. Over time, successful performance may support expansion into a broader Deputy Treasurer mandate.

Responsibilities

1. Treasury Governance and Regulatory Readiness
- Co-own (with subject matter experts) and continuously enhance Treasury’s governance framework, including policies , standards, procedures, management committees, change governance, issue management, and control documentation.
- Set minimum standards for Treasury methodologies, assumptions, models, controls, documentation, management reporting, and evidence retention, while partnering with accountable subject matter experts on implementation.
- Lead Treasury’s regulatory readiness program and serve as the senior Treasury lead for Federal Reserve and California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation examinations and supervisory engagement.
- Own Treasury-related regulatory remediation plans, including root-cause assessment, target-state design, milestones, evidence, management escalation, and sustainable closure; secure temporary or dedicated support when examination or remediation activity requires additional capacity.
- Lead Treasury’s engagement with the second and third lines of defense, including Enterprise Risk Management, Model Risk Management, Internal Audit, and other control partners.
- Monitor regulatory developments and industry practices, translate them into implications for the Bank, and advise the Treasurer and senior management on required actions and strategic choices.

2. Enterprise Capital and Liquidity Stress Testing
- Assume full accountability for the Bank’s capital stress testing program, including methodology, scenario design, assumptions, model and process governance, results integration, documentation, challenge, approvals, and executive communication.
- Lead the existing capital stress testing team and establish a clear operating model, decision rights, quality standards, development priorities, and talent plan.
- Own liquidity stress testing methodology and governance, while recurring production and execution remain with the Shanghai team and other designated subject matter experts.
- Further integrate capital and liquidity stress testing into a coherent enterprise framework that identifies vulnerabilities, connects stress outcomes to management actions, and informs contingency planning and risk appetite.
- Ensure stress testing appropriately incorporates balance sheet, earnings, credit, market, deposit, funding, liquidity, capital, and strategic assumptions from relevant functions.
- Lead senior management review and effective challenge of scenarios, assumptions, results, limitations, and proposed management actions.
- Drive progressive enhancement of stress testing capabilities in line with the Bank’s size, complexity, risk profile, and evolving supervisory expectations.

3. Strategic Planning and Forward-Looking Forecasting
- Lead an integrated, multi-year forward-looking planning process for the balance sheet, capital, liquidity, funding, and related earnings implications.
- Create a single Treasury planning view that incorporates the appropriate data, assumptions, and projections from Financial Planning & Analysis, Investor Relations, Asset Liability Management, senior management, business units, and risk partners.
- Establish planning calendars, ownership, assumption governance, reconciliation standards, controls, and executive review forums.
- Ensure baseline forecasts and stress scenarios are internally consistent and provide a clear view of capacity, constraints, trade-offs, and required management actions.
- Provide independent challenge of growth, deposit, funding, margin, capital, liquidity, and balance sheet assumptions, with transparent documentation of key judgments and sensitivities.
- Use planning outputs to support ALCO decisions, strategic initiatives, risk appetite, capital deployment, funding strategy, liquidity positioning, and management communications.

4. Committee Leadership and Executive Communication
- Present monthly to the Asset Liability Committee (ALCO) on governance, stress testing, regulatory readiness, forward-looking planning, key risks, and recommended actions.
- Present to the Risk Oversight Committee and the Board or its committees as needed, with increasing exposure as the role develops.
- Lead Treasury’s committee engagement, shaping decision-ready materials that translate technical analysis into clear implications, choices, risk tolerances, triggers, and management actions.
- Promote effective challenge, clear accountability, timely escalation, disciplined minutes and action tracking, and demonstrable closure of decisions.

5. Leadership and Organizational Development
- Provide direct leadership to the capital stress testing team, initially comprising a senior team lead and professionals across multiple levels.
- Clarify responsibilities between methodology ownership, governance, production, validation, review, and approval across Pasadena, Shanghai, and partner functions.
- Build scalable analytical capacity through development of existing team members and, as warranted, a Treasury rotational analyst, dedicated Shanghai analytical support, temporary remediation support, or additional headcount.
- Develop a culture of intellectual rigor, constructive challenge, clear documentation, accountability, continuous improvement, and strong cross-functional partnership.
- Serve as a senior advisor to the Treasurer and contribute thought leadership across Treasury priorities beyond the role’s direct programs.
- Partner with the Treasury Head of Data to establish clear data governance rules to facilitate effective analysis across the Treasury function as well as the wider bank.

Initial Mandate and Role-Evolution Milestones
Phase
Primary mandate

Establish
Confirm the target operating model, decision rights, inventory of methodologies and processes, team accountabilities, regulatory priorities, and an integrated roadmap.
Clear ownership, approved standards, prioritized gaps, stable governance calendar, and transparent milestones.

Integrate
Take full ownership of capital stress testing; establish liquidity stress testing methodology and governance; connect stress testing with forward-looking planning and ALCO decisions.
Consistent assumptions and scenarios, effective challenge, timely deliverables, strong documentation, and decision-useful results.

Elevate
Shift the programs from compliance-oriented execution to proactive thought leadership, with forward-looking insights, early-warning indicators, and credible management actions.

Expand
Subject to performance and organizational need, assume broader enterprise and Deputy Treasurer responsibilities over time.
Trusted representation of the Treasurer, broader ALCO leadership, selective Board exposure, and accountability beyond the initial functional mandate.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field; an advanced degree or professional designation is preferred.
- 15+ years of progressive experience in bank Treasury, capital management, liquidity risk, stress testing, financial planning, risk management, regulatory affairs, or relevant financial services advisory roles.
- Demonstrated leadership of capital planning or enterprise stress testing, including scenario design, methodology governance, forecasting, documentation, management challenge, and executive or regulatory communication.
- Strong knowledge of bank capital, liquidity, balance sheet management, asset liability management, funding, earnings forecasting, and the interdependencies among these areas.
- Substantial experience with U.S. bank regulatory expectations and supervisory examinations, including effective management of remediation programs.
- Proven ability to lead senior professionals and complex, cross-functional programs through influence as well as direct authority.
- Exceptional executive communication skills, including the ability to translate complex analysis into clear decisions, risks, and actions for ALCO, senior management, regulators, and Board audiences.
- Demonstrated judgment, integrity, intellectual curiosity, and willingness to challenge assumptions constructively.

Success in this role requires a leader who can move fluidly between technical depth and executive judgment. The individual must be able to set the standard, build alignment across functions, develop a strong team, anticipate regulatory expectations, and convert integrated capital, liquidity, and balance sheet analysis into practical management decisions. The strongest candidate will combine practitioner credibility with the thought leadership and communication skills needed to help Treasury mature as the Bank grows in size and complexity.

The role serves as a key advisor in evaluating tax-advantaged investment opportunities, assessing project risks and returns, structuring transactions, and monitoring portfolio performance to maximize after-tax economics and ensure realization of expected tax benefits.
The successful candidate will possess strong project finance and/or tax equity investment expertise, including the ability to evaluate complex partnership structures, model tax and cash flow outcomes, conduct comprehensive due diligence, and actively manage investments throughout their lifecycle.

Responsibilities

Investment Underwriting, Project Finance & Financial Modeling
- Lead comprehensive underwriting and due diligence of tax credit investment opportunities, with particular emphasis on renewable energy ITC and tax equity transactions.
- Assess project finance fundamentals, including sponsor strength, developer track record, construction risk, operating risk, revenue stability, capital structure, and financing assumptions.
- Build, maintain, and enhance complex financial models to evaluate projected tax benefits, cash flows, partnership economics, internal rates of return (IRR), return on investment (ROI), and after-tax returns.
- Perform detailed sensitivity analyses and stress testing across key variables including energy production, construction schedules, tax credit delivery, recapture risk, operating performance, and changes in tax law.

- Evaluate transaction risks and develop recommendations regarding investment sizing, pricing, structuring, and approval.
- Prepare investment committee memoranda, executive summaries, and recommendation packages for senior management.

- Review and negotiate financial provisions of partnership agreements, operating agreements, financing documents, and tax equity structures.
- Ensure investment documentation appropriately protects expected tax benefits, cash distributions, indemnification rights, and reporting requirements.
- Monitor transaction milestones and closing deliverables to ensure timely execution.

Portfolio Monitoring & Asset Management

- Review quarterly and annual financial statements, tax reporting packages, compliance certifications, engineering reports, operating metrics, and investor communications.
- Monitor construction progress, mechanical completion milestones, placed-in-service dates, tax credit qualification requirements, and project performance relative to underwriting assumptions.
- Evaluate actual versus projected tax credits, cash distributions, production performance, operating expenses, debt service coverage, and overall investment returns.
- Identify emerging project, tax, compliance, operational, or counterparty risks and develop mitigation strategies.

Branch Operations Lead

Location

US-WA-Bellevue

Job ID

2026-13554

Category

Branch Banking

Position Type

Full-Time

Introduction

Since 1973, East West Bank has served as a pathway to success. With over 110 locations across the U.S. and Asia, we are the premier financial bridge between the East and West. Our teams of experienced, multi-cultural professionals help guide businesses and community members on both sides of the Pacific looking to explore new markets and create new opportunities, and our sustained growth and expertise in industries like real estate, entertainment and media, private equity and venture capital, and high-tech help build sustainable businesses and expand our associates’ potential for career advancement.

Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

Overview

Being the next generation Branch Operations Lead at East West Bank means you are part of a world-class team that focuses on delivering a high quality, high-touch, and high-tech relationship banking experience across all customer touchpoints.

As a Branch Operations Lead, you will play a key role in:
- Assisting customers with their financial needs such as cash withdrawals, deposits, transfers, and loan payment across different platforms (online and mobile)
- Supervising the junior staff in the branch and providing guidance and approvals as needed
- Supporting the Assistant Branch Manager in leading the branch team to achieve sales, service, and operational excellence.

We will help you grow your career at East West Bank by providing you with ongoing training to expand your business knowledge, grow your digital acumen, and build long-lasting relationships with our customers.

Responsibilities

- Demonstrate strong customer service skills to assist customers with their financial needs; resolve escalated client complaints/issues promptly and effectively
- Provide support for branch customers by offering a wide range of bank products and services, including safe deposit box management, merchant/vault and ATM processing, foreign currency exchange and new account opening
- Train junior branch staff to effectively identify referral and sales opportunities and ensure they are compliant with bank policies and procedures.
- Refer customers to Business Relationship Managers and/or Financial Consultants for needs assessment to cross-sell bank products
- Expert in using digital resources and technologies to optimize clients’ digital banking experience
- Inform and educate clients on how to conduct simple transactions through convenient banking options (such as online banking, mobile banking, and ATMs)
- Provide back up support to the Assistant Branch Manager including branch certifications and audits
- May perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

- High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required; Bachelor’s degree preferred
- 3+ years of customer service, teller, or sales experience within the banking and/or financial service industry
- Strong working knowledge of branch operations required
- Familiarity with standard branch technology and teller equipment
- Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and customer-service skills

Applicants must have legal authorization to work in the United States.  We do not offer visa sponsorship at this time.

Compensation

The base pay range for this position is USD $26.00/Hr. - USD $29.00/Hr. Exact offers will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

jobs.description:
HR Business Partner

Location

US-NY-New York

Job ID

2026-13184

Category

Human Resources

Position Type

Full-Time

Introduction

Since 1973, East West Bank has served as a pathway to success. With over 110 locations across the U.S. and Asia, we are the premier financial bridge between the East and West. Our teams of experienced, multi-cultural professionals help guide businesses and community members on both sides of the Pacific looking to explore new markets and create new opportunities, and our sustained growth and expertise in industries like real estate, entertainment and media, private equity and venture capital, and high-tech help build sustainable businesses and expand our associates’ potential for career advancement.

Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

Overview

We are currently seeking a mid to senior-level HR Business Partner. This role will serve as the primary business partner to several business units and their associates. The incumbent will provide their client groups HR thought leadership and guidance to leadership and people managers on all people related matters. This may include but not limited to providing proactive, innovative, and customer-focused HR solutions that are tailored to the needs of their client groups but aligned with company’s standards and practices. The incumbent is also responsible for leading the key HR programs at their client groups, e.g., talent management/development, goal setting & performance management, consultation on employee relation issues, benefit administration, and building an inclusive culture in alignment with corporate value and corporate culture. They are also responsible for developing credible and trusting relationships with senior leaders, managers and employees.

Responsibilities

- Develops strong strategic working relationships with client groups and their teams to build an understanding of the business and their organization’s strengths and areas of opportunity, and maintains efficient level of business knowledge.
- Provides tailored coaching, consultation, guidance, and recommendations to client groups on all people related matters, and ensures alignment with our business strategies and workforce plan while maintaining our company culture and adhering to our company’s standards, policies, procedures, and practices.
- Implements and champions company-wide HR programs, policies, procedures and practices, HR initiatives, and develops solutions through organizational development.
- Drives annual HR processes, such as goal setting, performance management, compensation planning, talent review and planning, succession planning, etc.
- Advises management with respect to employee relations and performance management issues, with an emphasis on early identification and resolution. This includes but not limited to facilitating corrective actions, conducting internal investigations, communicating outcomes and recommendations to relevant stakeholders in accordance with stated corporate objectives and federal, state and local legal requirements.
- Partners with Center of Excellence on specialized HR areas including talent acquisition, compensation, benefits, training, employee engagement and HRIS to foster employee engagement and ensure positive employee experience.
- Partners with senior leadership in all business functions to ensure consistent practices, procedures, and HR strategies are being executed smoothly.
- Gathers and analyzes data to assess the effectiveness of HR initiatives and provides suggestions on enhancements, if applicable.
- Participates in and/or leads projects that advance our HR service delivery.
- Stays up-to-date in federal, state and local employment regulations.
- May perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources Management, Business or related field, or equivalent combination of training and experience is required.
- 8+ years of progressive HR experience with 4+ years in a generalist, or HR business partner capacity.
- Human Resources experience with banking industry is preferred, experience and knowledge in commercial lending is highly desired.
- General knowledge of U.S. employment laws and HR best practice is a must; Proven experience with multi-state HR is preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to maintain confidential information.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite; Intermediate to advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills are desired.
- Demonstrated ability to work with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Strong interpersonal communication skills.
- Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a team environment and across all organizational levels.
- Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment.
- Ability to work independently with minimum supervision while keeping relevant stakeholders up-to-date on his/her work
- Ability to read, analyze and interpret policies, procedures and other business practices, guidelines, and documents.
